clue.text: German writer pens long work of horror

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the writer's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist
to long is to pine, yearn

explanation.surface: A German author writes a lengthy horror novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like the writer's verb, but it means encloses. Schiller is the German poet and dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller that sends shivers down the reader's back is a classic description of a horror story.

clue.text: Phasing out of smallest British coin imminent

parts.note: P is short for penny, the smallest British coin
phasing out something is ending it

explanation.surface: The withdrawal of the penny from circulation is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awaiting decision or about to happen is said to be forthcoming, coming soon.

clue.text: Invalid taken to a hot stream

parts.note: null means void, invalid
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A sick person is brought to a warm spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' suggests a sick person, but it is the adjective, NULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullah is an Indian word for a watercourse or ravine with a stream.

clue.text: Actors missing for Tom Hanks movie

parts.note: the actors in a production are its cast
missing means away, absent

explanation.surface: Performers absent from a Tom Hanks film.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2000 film in which Hanks plays a man stranded on a desert island bears this title.

clue.text: French artist's singular entry

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A French painter's one and only debut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in, an entrance.

clue.text: Scousers wanting meat, then 'escargot' served up after dessert

indicators.note: after places the snail piece behind the dessert in the answer

parts.note: liver is an offal meat
pud is British slang for pudding, dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: escargot is French for snail

explanation.surface: Liverpool folk demand a meat course, then snails brought to the table after pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns SNAIL into LIANS, as this is a down clue. Scousers are people from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouser is the nickname for a native of Liverpool, the formal demonym being the answer.

clue.text: Regular offering as Sunday treat, principally?

definitions.text: Regular offering as Sunday treat, principally?

indicators.note: principally, read as 'by the principal letters', picks the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The usual Sunday treat is offered up.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast dinner is the traditional British Sunday lunch, a weekly treat.

clue.text: Brief problem, perhaps, for tough guy

definitions.meaning: a brief is a legal case, and a problematic one is a difficult case
a tough, uncompromising person, often a criminal

explanation.definitionFit: A difficult legal matter is literally a tricky case, while the compound is slang for a rough, hardened man.

clue.text: Learns manoeuvres on A-Team

indicators.note: manoeuvres says these letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up drills alongside the A-Team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges LEARNS into RSENAL, set beside A. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is an English Premier League football side, a team.

clue.text: A pale student's ordered nibbles

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: here the S of the possessive counts as a letter, giving the plural spelling

explanation.surface: A wan undergraduate has asked for some snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges A PALE STUDENTS; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Salted nuts are classic bar snacks, the nibbles served with drinks.

clue.text: Following directions, travel through Spanish town

parts.note: S and E are the compass directions south and east
to travel is to go
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Sticking to the signposts, a tourist passes through a town in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Segovia is a historic city in central Spain famous for its Roman aqueduct.

clue.text: A country boy turns to welcome a spiritual leader

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the reversed run receives the second a inside it
turns says the first stretch is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rural youth changes so as to greet a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses A MALI LAD to DALILAMA, and 'to welcome a' puts the second A in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of Tibetan Buddhism is a revered religious figure.

clue.text: Bird goes west in winter, generally

indicators.note: goes west says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird migrates west in the cold season, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes west' means read leftwards, as in an across clue: TERGE in wiNTER GEnerally turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Get even with cleric, in time

indicators.note: in says the cleric goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A clergyman settles a score in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: To get revenge on someone is to pay them back, settle the score.

clue.text: Royal family has food brought over round front of palace

indicators.note: round says the word has goes around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter
brought over says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A royal household has meals carried around the front of the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Habsburgs were the ruling dynasty of Austria and the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: Big woman developing in stages

indicators.note: developing says the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A large woman is growing bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A female giant is an exceptionally large woman.

clue.text: Individual detective's first to testify in court

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; with the 's it gives DIS

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter

explanation.surface: A police officer's the first to give evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means separate, individual.

clue.text: Clear front of my slippery path, covered in treacherous ice

indicators.note: covered in says the earlier pieces sit inside the jumbled ice
treacherous signals the letters of ice are unreliable, rearranged
front of picks the first letter
slippery signals the letters of path slide into a new order

explanation.surface: Plainly, the start of my slippery path is coated in dangerous ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' rearranges the path letters and 'treacherous' the ice letters, split so that 'covered in' can wrap them round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic statement is forceful and unmistakable, clear.

clue.text: Everything I wanted dealer ultimately installed inside old Austin

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: installed inside says the last letter goes within the self word

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter

explanation.surface: I got all I wanted when the dealer installed it inside my old car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Austin Allegro was a British family car of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allegro was a model made by British car maker Austin.

clue.text: A learner bound to suffer setback in Spanish course

indicators.note: a setback sends things back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: L is the learner sign on British cars
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A trainee is sure to face a reversal in a Spanish class.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'course' is part of a meal, not a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a rice dish from Valencia, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Seaman meets shellfish seller not initially supplying seafood?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Molly Malone sold cockles and mussels in the Dublin song

explanation.surface: A sailor meets a fishmonger who seems not to be supplying fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Irish song 'Cockles and Mussels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Something tiresome concerning 24

definitions.note: the answer to 24 across is a scold, a shrewish woman

parts.note: a drag is a bore, something tiresome
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A boring matter regarding the clue next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is slang for a fierce, domineering woman, a scold.

clue.text: Gem set in ring is right

indicators.note: set in says the right piece is placed inside, as a gem in a setting

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: A jewel mounted in a ring looks correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests jewellery, but it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem formed in an oyster.

clue.text: Sat for artist, showing self-control? Not!

indicators.note: the exclamation says the self, I, is not there

parts.note: poised means composed, showing self-control

explanation.surface: Someone modelled for a painter, appearing composed, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not!' removes the self, I, from POISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to model, to sit for a painter.

clue.text: Scold a good worker after some time?

indicators.note: after puts the worker pieces behind the time word

parts.note: a term is a set period of time
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Tell off a good worker after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a quarrelsome, overbearing woman, one who nags.

clue.text: Hurt by a foreign weapon

parts.note: stung means hurt
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Wounded by an alien weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun is an electroshock device used as a weapon.

clue.text: Provides explanation for German financial disasters

parts.note: losses are financial setbacks

explanation.surface: Someone explains the money crises of a German.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to add notes explaining it.

clue.text: Stopped playing, having broken record United overturned

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means playing, being performed

indicators.note: overturned says the letters are turned upside down into a new order

explanation.surface: A team stopped playing after losing its record, with United overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontinued means ceased, brought to an end.
